questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a different culture to the European and that the academic level was good and the people spoke English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The best decision I have done at university level.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I have to do a bit of emails to KU staff concerning the need for an English test (don’t need one to go to Singapore from CPH)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The NUS is really really good to send emails in the whole process and answer extremely quickly to any questions I had. NUS law did also do a lunch for all law exchange students in the first week

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to apply before for housing and it is not everybody that gets housing by NUS due to high demand by the majority does get accommodation at “PGPR” which is were must exchange students get housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There is no meal plan at PGPR, but a lot of the other accommodation options has meal plans. 
There is really cheap food stalls at pgpr so I just bought my meals there. 
There is a kitchen at the each floor in pgpr but is cheaper just to buy the food from the stalls

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That is it nice to have a AC in their room but not every room has it in pgpr but many just buy a portable one.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy just follow the emails from NUS

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply and then you get an email that lets you pay for the whole stay and then a new email a few weeks up to the stay that explains the on site process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always write and emails to them and they have a office at pgpr

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got 3 out of 4 classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
That you should take at least one intensive course because the semester is very intense, so you don’t have time to read up on everything if you have all exams at the end of the semester. 
Also read the material during the semester because the reading week is short before the exams in law at NUS.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
There is some big gaps in the academic levels in the courses in NUS 
I did maritime law which was a really higely advanced course. I also did Singapore legal history which was very easy to follow and not that hard academically

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: On an overall level the teaching style is the same. What is different is that you can grade for your class participation that has and impact in the final grade. Normally 10%.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Maritime law
Singapore legal history 
International water law 
Law of marine insurance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maritime law if the interest is there. Otherwise the legal history is a good course to get an overall understanding of Singapore history.

questions.answer:
Not really any. See the answer for former students and you get a good picture of the overall costs. 
Grab in Singapore is expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is cheap in the hawker center but beer is expensive. 
Transport is a bit expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is something for everyone at NUS

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
More or less anything you could imagine. 
NUS is really good at sending emails out to information students about upcoming events and activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do a sport and from there meet people. It is a nice way to meet new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travelling! Go around in south east Asia. It is really cheap and short destination to a lot of places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. By upon to new things and food and you will be absolute fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
The NUS clubs and by approaching in between classes 
And so the buddy program NUS sets up

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly people are and nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go travelling. 
By open to new things. 
Remember to enjoy it well you are there

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: NUS is really strict and sends a lot of emails. However NUS is more strict on paper then in reality so don’t be to scared about the emails.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new view of the world I got.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maritime law.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
